name: Northpass Tower
summary: Northpass Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated in the northern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands along the road to Quel'Thalas. Shattered during the Third War, it still overlooks the northern road toward the elven lands.

sections.title: Northern Sentinel
sections.body: Built by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to guard the vital thoroughfare leading north into Quel'Thalas, Northpass Tower was reduced to a broken shell during the Scourge invasion. Despite its shattered stonework, the tower's elevated position retains immense tactical value, overlooking the blight-choked frontier between Stratholme's blighted outskirts and the distant elven lands.

sections.title: A Silent Watch
sections.body: No garrison mans the tower today. Its broken walls stand along a road now haunted by the Scourge, a reminder of the watch Lordaeron once kept over the route to Quel'Thalas.

faq.q: What was Northpass Tower originally built for?
faq.answer: It was originally erected as an observation post by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to monitor the northern road leading toward the elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas.

faq.q: Why is Northpass Tower in ruins?
faq.answer: It was destroyed alongside the rest of Lordaeron's northern defenses during the Scourge invasion in the Third War, leaving behind only cracked masonry and scaffolding.

faq.q: Does anyone hold Northpass Tower now?
faq.answer: No. The tower was destroyed alongside Lordaeron's northern defenses during the Scourge invasion and now stands as an empty ruin along the road north.

faq.q: Where does the road past Northpass Tower lead?
faq.answer: The road heads north directly toward the Thalassian border and the southern territory of Quel'Thalas.

angles.text: Northpass Tower is one of the fallen bastions of Lordaeron, a broken sentinel on the road to the elven lands.
For the Horde, ruins like Northpass Tower show how thoroughly the Scourge broke the defenses of the northern kingdoms.
